title: Route table (the HTTP envelope of every message)
description: Not a message: the transport around them. examples/routes.json lists every publish-v1 route - method, path, who sends it, which credential and headers it takes, and which schema file the body and each answer follow. Everything is plain JSON over HTTPS: no signing, no compression, no wrapping beyond the headers named here. Every non-2xx answer with an `error` code follows error.response.schema.json. The provider test checks that each route here exists in OpenResults' router.

path.description: Phoenix route pattern; :slug is the tournament slug, URL-encoded.

senders.description: Which programs call this route today. Empty: exposed, no current caller.

auth.description: The Authorization: Bearer credentials accepted. none: an open route. operator: the server-wide ingest token. installation: an orik_ key (only with OPENRESULTS_PUBLIC_PUBLISHING=enabled; only for tournaments minted for it). relay: an orrk_ key, live route of its own tournament only.

headers.description: Other request headers and what they carry.

public_publishing_only.description: true: the route exists only when the server runs with public publishing enabled; otherwise Phoenix's own 404.

request.description: Schema file of the JSON body, or null for no body.

responses.description: HTTP status -> schema file (or a note when the body is not one of ours).
